passages.scripture: A few days later Jesus went back to Capernaum. And when the people heard that He was home, they gathered in such large numbers that there was no more room, not even outside the door, as Jesus spoke the word to them.

lines.text: A few days later Jesus went back to Capernaum — Capernaum was a town by the Sea of Galilee where Jesus had taught before.
And the people heard that Jesus was home.
So the people gathered in such large numbers that there was no more room.
There was no more room, not even outside the door — the crowd filled the house and spilled outside the house.
Jesus spoke the word to them — this word is God's message, the good news that His kingdom has come near.

passages.scripture: Then a paralytic was brought to Him, carried by four men.

lines.text: Then a paralyzed man was brought to Jesus.
Four men carried the paralyzed man to Jesus.

passages.scripture: Since they were unable to get to Jesus through the crowd, they uncovered the roof above Him, made an opening, and lowered the paralytic on his mat.

lines.text: There was a paralyzed man.
The paralyzed man was lying on a mat.
A crowd was around Jesus.
So the four men could not bring the paralyzed man to Jesus.
So the four men uncovered the roof above Jesus.
And the four men made an opening through the roof.
And then the four men lowered the mat down through the opening.

passages.scripture: When Jesus saw their faith, He said to the paralytic, “Son, your sins are forgiven.”

lines.text: Jesus saw the faith of the four men — they were so convinced Jesus would heal the paralyzed man that they were willing to overcome obstacles to get him into Jesus’ presence.
Jesus is called the “Everlasting Father” — He cares for His people like a father, so He calls the paralyzed man “son”.
The paralyzed man was not an earthly son of Jesus.
Jesus said to the paralyzed man, “Son, your sins are forgiven.”
God forgave the paralyzed man’s sins — by the time Jesus finished speaking, every sin of his was forgiven.

passages.scripture: But some of the scribes were sitting there and thinking in their hearts, “Why does this man speak like this? He is blaspheming! Who can forgive sins but God alone?”

lines.text: Some of the scribes were sitting there.
The scribes were thinking in their hearts — silently, to themselves.
The scribes thought, “Why does this man — Jesus — speak like this?”
The scribes thought, “Jesus is blaspheming!”
To blaspheme is to insult God — for example, by claiming to do what only God can do.
The scribes thought, “Who can forgive sins but God alone?”
The scribes were right about this: only God can forgive sins — but they did not realize that Jesus Christ is God over all.

passages.scripture: At once Jesus knew in His spirit that they were thinking this way within themselves. “Why are you thinking these things in your hearts?” He asked.

lines.text: At once Jesus knew what the scribes were thinking within themselves.
Jesus knew it in His spirit — no one told Him, and the scribes had not said a word.
Jesus asked the scribes, “Why are you thinking these things in your hearts?”
Only God can see what is hidden in people’s hearts — and Jesus saw it.
